# PROGRAMmable CONTROLLERS  

## Part 1: General information  

# 1 Scope  

This Part of IEC 61131 applies to programmable controllers (PLC) and their associated peripherals such as programming and debugging tools (PADTs), human-machine interfaces (HMs), etc., which have as their intended use the control and command of machines and industrial processes.  

PLCs and their associated peripherals are intended to be used in an industrial environment and may be provided as open or enclosed equipment. If a PLC or its associated peripherals are intended for use in other environments, then the specific requirements, standards and installation practices for those other environments must be additionally applied to the PLC and its associated peripherals.  

The functionality of a programmable controller can be performed as well on a specific hardware and software platform as on a general-purpose computer or a personal computer with industrial environment features. This standard applies to any products performing the function of PLCs and/or their associated peripherals. This standard does not deal with the functional safety or other aspects of the overall automated system. PLCs, their application programme and their associated peripherals are considered as components of a control system.  

Since PLCs are component devices, safety considerations for the overall automated system including installation and application are beyond the scope of this Part. However, PLC safety as related to electric shock and fire hazards, electrical interference immunity and error detecting of the PLC-system operation (such as the use of parity checking, self-testing diagnostics, etc.), are addressed. Refer to IEC 60364 or applicable national/local regulations for electrical installation and guidelines.  

This Part of IEC 61131 gives the definitions of terms used in this standard. It identifies the principal functional characteristics of programmable controller systems.

### 4.6.3 Writing the application programme

#### Generating the application programme
The application programme may be entered via alphanumeric or symbolic keyboards and, when menu-driven displays are, or a graphical programme entry is, used via cursor keys, joystick, mouse, etc. All programme and data entries are generally checked for validity and internal consistency in such a way that the entry of incorrect programmes and data is minimized.

#### Displaying the application programme
During application programme generation, all instructions are displayed immediately, statement by statement or segment by segment (in the case of a monitor or other large display). In addition, the complete programme can generally be printed. If alternative representation of programming language elements is available, then the display representation is generally user-selectable.

### 4.6.4 Automated system start-up

#### Loading the application programme
The generated programme resides either in the memory of the programmable controller or in the memory of the PADT. The latter requires a programme transfer via down-load or memory cartridge insertion into the programmable controller before start-up.

#### Accessing the memory
During start-up or trouble-shooting operations, the application programme and application data storage are accessed by the PADT as well as by the processing unit to allow programme monitoring, modification and correction. This may be done on line (i.e. while the PLC-system is controlling the machine/process).

### d) Adapting the programmable controller system
Typical functions for adapting the PLC-system to the machine/process to be controlled are:
1. test functions which check the sensors and actuators connected to the PLC-systems (for example, forcing the outputs of the PLC-system);
2. test functions which check the operation of the programme sequence (for example, setting of flags and forcing the inputs);
3. setting or resetting of variables (for example, timers, counters, etc.).

#### Indicating the automated system status
The ability to provide information about the machine/process and the internal status of the PLC-system and of its application programme facilitates the start-up and debugging of a PLC application. Typical means are:
1. status indication for inputs/outputs;
2. indication/recording of status changes of external signals and internal data;
3. scan time/execution times monitoring;
4. real-time visualization of programme execution and data processing;
5. fuse/short-circuit protection status indicators.

}}}{~{} (b) Architecture of the programmable controller system

A modular construction in conjunction with suitable internal self-tests allowing rapid fault identification may provide enhancements in the area of maintainability of the PLC-system and therefore of the availability of the automated system. Techniques such as redundancy and fault tolerance may also be considered for special applications.
c) Design, testing and maintenance of the application programme

The application programme is a key component of the overall automated system. Most programmable controllers provide enough computing power to permit implementation of diagnostic functions in addition to the minimum control function. Machine/process behaviour modelling and subsequent identification of faulty conditions should be considered.

Adequate testing of the application programme is mandatory. Every modification implies proper design and testing so that the overall availability and reliability are not impaired. The programme documentation shall be maintained and annotated accordingly.
d) Installation and service conditions

PLC-systems are typically of rugged design and intended for general-purpose service. However, as for any equipment, the more stressing the service conditions, the worse is the reliability, and benefit in this area may be expected when permitted service conditions are better than the normal service conditions specified in IEC 61131-2. Some applications may require consideration of special packaging, cooling, electrical noise protection, etc., for reliable operation.}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}

he United States has always set high goals for itself when hosting vulnerable communities, and given a clear path to reach equality and dignity. We should have the same aspirations for Afghan refugees and prevent wrongful deportations amid already difficult circumstances.

Afghan refugees recognize that now is the time to consolidate and resettle safely in the United States, and to contribute on equal footing to our nation.

Congress can help by passing the Afghan Community Reintegration Act, which was issued a bipartisan letter from Marie Hodges, head of the Afghan Women’s Organization.

It is time for the United States to reconnect with Afghan people.

Americans want nothing more than for this country to right its wrongs.
Majority Leader Steny Hoyer

video Digital Migration Initiative Assistance
May 4, 2022

The need to quickly get Afghan refugees who have escaped poverty and war into work and housing, and help them make the next steps to integration. Secretary Mayorkas and I have worked across governments and interagency partners to increase access to digital inclusion and training support for Afghan refugees in the United States.

For instance, we are supporting the President’s initiative to provide Digital Migration Initiative assistance, which is providing critical help to too many Afghans get digital access to build prosperity in their own communities.

And we are working with the State Department to increase the private affiliate providers interested in engaging Afghan refugees as Digital Provisors.

We continue to help a number of Afghan refugees in the department, like masonry worker Eunice, who sells frescoes at what she now says is Street Art Once Upon a Time.

Eunice now lives on her own salary with her three children. Multiple agencies have supported Eunice throughout her 20-year career.

I came to work my own path after saving to join the Peace Corps. I never imagined my country would send me this far from home, but this experience has shaped me in ways I could not have imagined.

She has told anyone who will listen.

There are many important factors to consider when choosing a programming language for your application. These include factors such as your hardware and software configuration, the application's complexity, the required level of performance, and the platform you wish to use.

In addition, there are many different programming languages available, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. When choosing a programming language, it is important to consider factors such as ease of learning, the developer community and industry standards, the language's implementation and functionality, and the language's popularity for other projects. There are many programming languages available, such as Java, C++, C#, and Python. Each of these languages has its own advantages and disadvantages. It is important to understand the strengths and weaknesses of each language when making a decision.

Some of the main factors to consider when choosing a programming language are:

1. Ease of Use: Some programming languages are easier to learn than others. It is important to consider the level of complexity and generalizability of the language when making a decision.

2. Community: Some programming languages have larger and more active communities than others. It is important to consider the availability of support and resources when choosing a programming language.

3. Platforms: Some platforms only support certain programming languages. It is important to consider the platforms available when choosing a programming language.

4. Performance: Some programming languages are better suited for particular types of applications, while others are better for other types of applications. Performance is an important factor to consider when choosing a programming language.

5. Tool and Framework Support: Some languages support particular tools and frameworks. It is important to consider the tools and frameworks available when choosing a programming language.

6. Industry Standards Compliance: Some languages support industry standards, while others do not. It is important to consider the industry standards compliance when making a decision.

7. Error Handling: Error handling is an important feature to consider when choosing a programming language. The language of the highest performance should be selected.

8. Multi-threaded and concurrent function support: Some languages support multi-threaded and concurrent function support. It is important to consider the type of applications that will be supported when choosing a programming language.

9. Debugging support: Some languages provide more robust and comprehensive debugging support. It is important to consider the type of applications that will be supported when choosing a programming language.

10. Portability: Some programming languages are more portable than others. It is important to consider the type of applications that will be supported when choosing a programming language.11.

Besides, the language of the program's execution speed and the amount of memory it consumes. Overall, the programming language should be selected based on the specific requirements of your application.

### 4.3 Caractéristiques de la fonction d'interface avec les capteurs et les actionneurs

#### a) Types de signaux d'entrée/de sortie

Les informations de statut et les données obtenues à partir de la machine/du processus sont acheminées vers le système E/S de l'automate programmable par des signaux binaires, numériques, incrémentiels ou analogiques. À l'inverse, les décisions et résultats déterminés par la fonction de traitement sont acheminés vers la machine/processus à l'aide de signaux binaires, numériques, incrémentiels ou analogiques appropriés. La grande variété de capteurs et d'actionneurs utilisés nécessite de prendre en charge un vaste éventail de signaux d'entrée et de sortie.

#### b) Caractéristiques du système d'entrée/de sortie

#### 4.2.3 Mémoire destinée au stockage des données de l'application

Le stockage du programme application fournit des emplacements mémoire pour stocker une série d'instructions dont l'exécution périodique ou sur événement détermine la progression de la machine ou du processus. Le stockage du programme application peut également fournir des emplacements mémoire pour stocker les valeurs initiales destinées à des données du programme application.

#### 4.2.4 Type de mémoire, capacité de la mémoire, utilisation de la mémoire

Différents types de mémoire sont utilisés: lecture/écriture (RAM), lecture seule (ROM), lecture programmable seule (PROM), lecture reprogrammable seule (EPROM/UV-PROM, EEPROM). La rétention de mémoire lors d'une mise hors service est réalisée par une sélection adaptée du type de mémoire (par exemple, EPROM, EEPROM) ou par l'utilisation d'une sauvegarde mémoire pour les mémoires volatiles (par exemple une batterie). La capacité mémoire concerne le nombre d'emplacements de mémoire en Koctets, qui sont réservés au stockage du programme application et des données de l'application. Les mesures de la capacité de mémoire sont les suivantes:

- capacité dans la configuration minimale utile;

- taille(s) des extensions incrémentales;

- capacité(s) à la/aux configuration(s) maximal(es).

Chaque fonction programmable utilisée par le programme d'application occupe des emplacements mémoire. Le nombre d'emplacements requis dépend en général des fonctions programmables et du type d'automate programmable.

Le stockage des données de l'application exige une capacité mémoire qui dépend de la quantité et du format des données stockées.
